evals.prompt: Our Claude contract-review service on Sonnet sends this on every request: a system prompt of about 9,000 characters of review instructions, then a 'reference' block with our 40,000-character clause library, then a line 'Today's date: {now}' appended to the end of that reference block, then 6 fixed few-shot examples (~12,000 characters), then the user's uploaded contract (varies per request). It's single-turn, roughly 2,000 requests a day. Where should the cache_control breakpoints go?
assertions: Flags that the per-request timestamp appended to the reference block makes that block dynamic and would cause every request to miss, and recommends moving it out of the cached prefix before caching
No recommended cached block contains dynamic content — the user's contract and the date stay outside every breakpoint
Shows an annotated messages/system structure with each cache_control placement marked and commented
Explains that a breakpoint caches the entire prefix up to and including that block, not just the block itself
Uses at most three breakpoints, one per logical boundary
Checks block sizes against the Sonnet minimum (~2,048 tokens) using ~4 characters per token before recommending a cache
Gives a cache strategy summary paragraph with what is cached, why, expected hit rate, and the dominant cost driver before and after
Does not invent prompt sections, request volumes, or models beyond those in the prompt
